card.name: "For" before treatment duration
card.fires_on: The word "for" (or the space just before a number) right after a dose or dosing frequency, where a length of treatment comes next, such as "for 2 years" or "for 14 days". Seen in animal studies and healthy-subject dosing.

modes.label: "for" after dose
modes.description: The word "for" follows a dose amount or daily rate and introduces how long it was given.
modes.example: posterior Y suture lines in the ocular lens were seen in dogs after treatment with 1, 8, and 16 mg/kg/day<< for>> 2 years.

modes.label: Space before duration number
modes.description: The pole fires on the gap just before a number of days or weeks that gives a duration.
modes.example: During controlled clinical trials in healthy subjects, once daily doses up to 320 mg of azilsartan medoxomil were administered for<< >>7 days and were well tolerated.

card.writes: It seems to push the model toward a number and time unit that gives the length of treatment.
card.plain: It marks the spot where a text is about to say how long a dose was given.
